headline: New MASS framework enables AI to recursively self-improve using collective intelligence
summary: A new framework called Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS) allows AI models to recursively improve themselves by distilling collective intelligence from multi-agent systems, boosting performance on complex research tasks.
details: AI can now recursively self-improve (RSI) using a new framework called Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS). This system allows the AI itself to act as its own optimizer and evaluator, pushing beyond humanity's accumulated knowledge.

Human experts often struggle to assess results and guide progress on non-verifiable tasks. MASS addresses this by enabling the model to become its own most capable supervisor, figuring out how to improve internally.

Inspired by how human societies expand capabilities through dividing work, combining ideas, and collective learning, MASS applies this concept. It allows a model to learn from its own 'team's' collective intelligence, which a single agent may not reliably exhibit.

MASS uses the same language model as the executor, optimizer, and evaluator. The optimizer searches for the best team workflow using feedback from the evaluator, then trains the executor on executions from the self-judged best team.

This process provides a self-supervision signal for recursive self-improvement by distilling the team's collective experience into the shared model. An inner loop optimizes the team's workflow, and an outer loop then updates model weights based on the optimized workflow executions.

To measure progress, external AI models like GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 assess the completed work. Their judgments are withheld from MASS, providing an independent measure of improvement in this self-supervised learning loop.

headline_marked: [[Open-source Microsoft Word reimplementation]] in pure Rust, with familiar UI and .docx support
headline: Open-source Microsoft Word reimplementation in pure Rust, with familiar UI and .docx support
summary: WordCraft is a fast, open-source word processor built in pure Rust, supporting the familiar ribbon UI, styles, track changes, and full .docx compatibility across all major desktop platforms and the browser.
details: WordCraft is an ambitious open-source project aiming to be a clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word, built entirely in pure Rust. Currently in alpha, it covers 88% of Word's ribbon features and is estimated to be 60% of the way to replacing Word for real work.

It offers a familiar Word workflow, including the ribbon, live Styles gallery, tables, track changes, references (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE), and mail merge. Design features like themes, paragraph spacing, watermarks, and dark mode are also supported.

The application runs natively on macOS, Windows, Linux, and BSD. It can also be used in the browser via WebAssembly. WordCraft reads and writes .docx files, ensuring compatibility with existing documents.

Beyond human interaction, WordCraft is designed to be driven by AI agents, offering specific tools like list_commands, execute, type_text, and inspect_document. This allows agents to check their work without relying on screenshots.

The project's roadmap details its path to beta, focusing on testing against real-world .docx files, maintaining charts and SmartArt through round trips, improving pagination accuracy, enhancing stability, and implementing native printing.
